topIssues.title: op/kona-node lite: follow both local_safe and safe heads from source
topIssues.author: geoknee
topIssues.body:
An op-node configured for lite mode (following a source instead of doing derivation itself) will currently set the local_safe head of the upstream safe head.

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/80804af288d016d28bf26e3b14e58679bb070d87/op-node/rollup/driver/driver.go#L550

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/80804af288d016d28bf26e3b14e58679bb070d87/op-node/rollup/engine/engine_controller.go#L1221-L1222

This can be problematic for interop, where sequencers run as lite CLs. In that setup, the local safe of the sequencer will lag the _actual_ local safe, since the unqualified `safe` label is delayed until interop verification finishes. This confuses the op-batcher, if it connects to the sequencer, since it expects local safe head progression after posting batch txs. It can erroneously enter a recovery mode where it loads more blocks than it should. 

We should update the engine controller to track both heads so the sync status of a lite CL lines up with that of a supernode.

topIssues.title: op-supernode: Prune Denylist on L1 Reorg and Alert
topIssues.author: axelKingsley
topIssues.body:
We need to ensure that whenever the Virtual Node responds to an L1 reorg, all downstream components prune data:

Chain Containers must prune their `Denylist` - if not, then a legitimate Unsafe chain could be denied inappropriately

Activities need to be notified via the same `Reset` callback already used. This is because they need to prune their verification results and logs.
Related: Related to: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19287

topPRs.title: sc-feat: policy engine staking ordering
topPRs.author: ashitakah
topPRs.body:
**PolicyEngineStaking** is a periphery contract that enables stake-aware transaction ordering in op-rbuilder.

Users deposit OP tokens and optionally link their stake to a beneficiary that receives ordering power. The contract maintains an aggregated, PE-optimized view of effective stake and last update timestamp per address in a single packed storage slot, allowing the Policy Engine to read stake data directly via state_by_block_hash() with O(1) lookups and no RPC calls.

topPRs.title: pure: add pure derivation pipeline in op-core/pure
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Adds `op-core/pure/` package implementing a pure function derivation pipeline
- `PureDerive()` takes L1 data + safe head state, returns derived L2 payload attributes — no I/O, no L2 state reads
- Post-Holocene only, with protocol modification: no overlapping span batches (eliminates L2 fetcher dependency)

## Design

Single pure function that loops over L1 blocks sequentially:
1. Apply system config updates from L1 receipts
2. Parse frames from batcher transactions
3. Assemble channels (Holocene single-channel strict-order model)
4. Decode and validate batches
5. Build payload attributes (L1 info deposit + user deposits + batch txs)
6. Generate empty batches when sequencer window expires

Reuses existing pure functions from `op-node/rollup/derive/` (frame parsing, channel assembly, batch decoding, deposit encoding, L1 block info). Fresh implementation for the orchestration layer.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `types.go` | L1Input, DerivedBlock, l2Cursor, BlockInfo adapter |
| `channels.go` | Holocene single-channel assembler |
| `batches.go` | Batch decoding, validation, empty batch generation |
| `attributes.go` | PayloadAttributes assembly |
| `derive.go` | `PureDerive()` entry point |
| `helpers_test.go` | Shared test utilities |

## Test plan

- [x] 31 unit tests covering all pipeline stages
- [x] Channel assembly: single-frame, multi-frame, new channel discards old, timeout, out-of-order
- [x] Batch validation: correct timestamp, wrong timestamp, epoch range, overlap rejection
- [x] Empty batch generation: window expiry detection, correct epoch advancement
- [x] Attributes assembly: epoch boundaries, same epoch, Holocene-specific fields
- [x] End-to-end: single batch, empty epochs, multiple channels/epochs, channel timeout, invalid batch skip
- [ ] Differential test against existing pipeline (follow-up)
